newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs higher in late Tokyo, sentiment remains firm.
newsitem.headline: JGBs higher in late Tokyo, sentiment remains firm.

text.p: Cash yen bonds and futures were higher in late trade on Monday as sentiment remained strong, traders said.

They said that given weak Tokyo stock prices, there were few investment alternatives. Newly launched domestic corporate straight bonds saw brisk sales on Monday, supporting Japanese government bonds (JGBs).

"Those who had been bearish on JGBs finally covered their shorts today as the Tokyo stock market did not rebound despite banks' restructuring plans last week," said a dealer at a long-term credit bank's securities unit.

Large-lot short-covering was detected in JGB futures in the afternoon, which was said to have come from foreign hedge funds, resulting in the key June futures contract's rise to a record high for any benchmark contract of 127.25, traders said.
The June ended at 127.19, up 0.32 from Friday's finish.
The yield of the benchmark three percent 182nd 10-year JGB stood at a record low of 2.090 percent at 0649 GMT. The yield ended at 2.120 percent on Friday.
Given record low yields in JGBs, seven corporations rushed to tap the primary corporate bond market on Monday.

Seven firms - NEC Corp, KDD, Sumitomo Chemical, Sumitomo Electric Industries, Sapporo Breweries, Aoki International and Chugoku Electric Power - launched straight bonds totalling about 250 billion yen on Monday, bond traders said.
"Some feared that the market might fail to absorb today's launches of straight corporate bonds. But sales of the new straights went fairly well," the dealer said.
The fact that investors currently prefer JGBs over any other yen bonds, including bank debentures, is also providing support, traders said.
